connection: The company names Rapoport as a co-founder, and a published interface patent names him as an inventor.
how_helpful: A focused enquiry could clarify why the first temporary electrode was developed, which inventions belong to it and how it was financed.
limits: This is a product-origin connection, not evidence of London use. A broad interface patent is not automatically a patent on the selected marketed component.
route: Use the company website to request a development-history contact. No personal introduction has been obtained.

connection: Morrell is associated with the original RNS trial and is named in the company’s RNS-specific clinical presentations.
how_helpful: Useful for the early clinical need, trial design, regulatory development and how chronic recordings changed follow-up.
limits: A company clinical perspective does not independently establish payer coverage or disclose the first investors. This is not a London visit lead.
route: NeuroPace’s Investor Day page publishes investors@neuropace.com; request routing to the appropriate clinical/development contact.

connection: Stanford describes his role in the brain-stethoscope development and Ceribell; he co-authored the device-specific economic paper, which publishes his contact.
how_helpful: He is relevant to invention origin, the clinical problem and the assumptions behind the economic case—not simply to EEG in general.
limits: He has a commercial connection to the company. A developer’s account should be checked against patents, trials and payer records; it does not establish London use.
route: jparvizi@stanford.edu is the corresponding-author address in the 2021 economic paper; verify it before outreach. A company research route is also listed.

connection: Magnus identifies Bentzley as a co-founder who co-developed SAINT at Stanford; its IP statement identifies licensed Stanford patents.
how_helpful: Useful for how the academic protocol became a product, what was licensed and the practical requirements of commercialization.
limits: He is a developer/company source, not an independent efficacy reviewer or evidence of a London clinic. Patent inventorship must come from the patent, not the founder title.
route: Use the Magnus provider/company enquiry route and ask for a development-history contact.

person: Professor Ludvic Zrinzo / UCLH-NHNN functional neurosurgery team
connection: The London methods paper documents ExAblate equipment and includes Zrinzo; the NHS profile confirms his local role and provides an administrative contact.
how_helpful: Useful for patient selection, comparison with DBS, treatment workflow, scanner/staff costs and barriers to UK adoption.
limits: The clinical team is not automatically a source for the manufacturer’s original private financing or patent negotiations. A published service does not guarantee an observation visit.
route: uclh.neurosurgery.admin@nhs.net for the consultant’s team, or treatment@queensquare.com via the service page; request an educational staff discussion.

person: Jane Symonds / Neurokinex ARC-EX and Pathfinder2 team
location: Hemel Hempstead and Gatwick; outside London
connection: Symonds is a named Pathfinder2 author with a Neurokinex Hemel Hempstead affiliation. Neurokinex identifies its ARC-EX study, and ONWARD lists its Hemel Hempstead and Gatwick centres for the exact product.
how_helpful: Ask about patient selection, session structure, therapist training, equipment/consumable costs, outcome measurement and how community rehabilitation is funded. This is direct device-study/provider experience, not a recommendation based only on general SCI expertise.
limits: The 2025 paper gives a historical affiliation, not a verified current appointment. Neurokinex discloses a shareholder interest in ONWARD; co-author Jenny Suggitt discloses ONWARD employment. Check claims against independent records. A provider cannot automatically answer original patent ownership or all early financing questions.
route: info@neurokinex.org; 0300 77 77 188. Request the current ARC-EX team or routing to the Pathfinder2 investigators, and ask whether an educational staff discussion is possible.

person: Spinal Research ARC-EX / Recovery Alliance programme team
connection: The charity funded Pathfinder2 and is running an ARC-EX device-loan programme with UK rehabilitation centres; its contact page confirms a London office.
how_helpful: Ask how the UK study and device-access programme were funded, which centres have direct experience, what evidence is needed for wider adoption, and how charity support differs from long-term payment.
limits: This is a funder and access-programme perspective, not a clinical examination or a promise of access to patients. Programme support is not proof of routine NHS coverage, and the charity has an interest in the programme’s success.
route: info@spinal-research.org; 0203 8247 400. Request the ARC-EX/Recovery Alliance programme team, rather than treating the office address as an invitation to visit.
